scope: S3 reviewed-C control and byte-identical Rust c837 trace repeat, followed by one normal-logging control; all outcomes retained.
test_order: A1: original Rust c837 trace run
A2: exact same signed Rust trace image
Normal logging: Rust c837 same source and pins, diagnostic features disabled

reviewed_c_control.scope: Reviewed C control between the first corrected Rust trace run and one byte-identical Rust repeat.

probe_changes: 1-second settle then 10-second host window before gateway traffic
record all completed cycles; final assertion requires each cycle20/20 and total200/200 gateway replies
source.unchanged_lifecycle: full esp_wifi init, passive scan, WPA2/DHCP, TSF check, disconnect/stop/deinit; power save disabled

limitations: C retains full Wi-Fi init, passive scan, stop and deinit on each cycle; Rust retains initialized PHY and driver across reconnects.
C uses ESP-IDF/lwIP and its default station MAC; Rust uses FoA/embassy/smoltcp and a randomized station MAC.
C uses normal IDF logging; Rust trace logs every FoA start/finish and packet metadata. Logging overhead is not matched.
Gateway count/512-byte payload/100ms interval/1s timeout are configured equally, but ping schedulers and payload-validation implementations differ.
No over-the-air capture was recorded. Results compare whole applications under nearby network conditions, not an isolated single-variable driver experiment.
The unchanged IDF configuration enables PHY calibration/data storage; the C application may update calibration data in NVS. Wi-Fi configuration itself uses RAM storage.

rust_trace_repeat.scope: S3 ten-cycle station validation with actual MAC completion metadata and station sequence assignment.

test_parameters.other_target_activity: Coordinated S3 window; root paused C3 station testing.

source.local_uncommitted_change: examples pins and lock select published FoA station sequence correction and smoltcp idempotent setter

mac_completion_trace.sequence_order: Completion header sequence, ordered by the paired start-event position, modulo 4096.

runs.final_device_state: Application failed after recorded cycles; see preserved failure metadata.

limitations: Packet boundary and MAC-completion logs expose different boundaries. Ok(n) reports driver success after n retries; it does not prove application processing by the peer.
A completion reports the final header and retry count, not each on-air retry or its Retry bit. No monitor-mode capture was taken.
The ten-cycle run is a bounded one-board/one-AP test; advancing sequence numbers prove the concrete assignment correction, not the cause of every earlier packet loss.

source.local_uncommitted_change: examples pins and lock select published FoA station sequence correction and smoltcp idempotent setter

limitations: This profile disables packet/MAC traces, so any missing reply cannot be correlated with a per-frame completion.
Source and dependency hashes equal the traced c837 image; profile-dependent compiled code and logging overhead differ.
One bounded control does not establish whether a changed result is caused by diagnostic overhead rather than run-to-run variation.
rust_normal_logging.final_device_state: Application panicked after connecting cycle1 and timing out before DHCP; no traffic stage or planned disconnect was reached.

conclusions: The reviewed C control achieved200/200 unique host replies and200/200 gateway replies with zero host duplicates.
Both traced Rust runs failed the final gateway assertion, with194/200 and199/200 gateway replies; the exact signed image was unchanged.
All traced generated frame sequences advanced and every queued start had a matching final endpoint completion.
The normal-logging control failed at DHCP before any ping traffic, so it cannot establish diagnostic-overhead effects on ping loss.
Differences in full Wi-Fi teardown, MAC identity, stack, calibration lifecycle, compiler and diagnostics prevent single-variable attribution from this bounded comparison.
